core_obligations: Deduce quasi-compactness of X from surjectivity of X_K to X, and quasi-separatedness of X by the affine-open criterion, since the base change of U cap V is quasi-compact and surjects onto U cap V (proof lines 2789-2797).

Write K as the colimit of its finitely generated k-subalgebras and use the descent of quasi-affineness through the resulting limit, possible because X is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, to find i with X_i quasi-affine (proof lines 2800-2805).

Choose a maximal ideal of A_i; the Nullstellensatz makes its residue field k' a finite extension of k, and the base change X_{k'} is a closed subscheme of X_i and hence quasi-affine (proof lines 2806-2811).
Conclude that X is quasi-affine by descending along the finite locally free morphism X_{k'} to X (proof lines 2812-2813).
proof_roadmap: Descend quasi-affineness along the colimit presentation of K (proof lines 2800-2805).
Reduce to a finite extension by the Nullstellensatz (proof lines 2806-2811).
Descend from the finite locally free cover (proof lines 2812-2813).
difficulty_reason: If X_K is quasi-affine for some field extension K/k, the lemma concludes that X is quasi-affine (statement lines 2782-2786). The proof is the same spreading-out pattern as for properness: surjectivity of X_K to X gives quasi-compactness of X, and the quasi-separatedness of X is deduced by separating affine opens upstairs, so that X may be assumed quasi-compact and quasi-separated (proof lines 2789-2797). Then K is written as the colimit of its finitely generated k-subalgebras, X_K is recognized as the limit of the base changes X_i, and quasi-affineness descends to some X_i; a maximal ideal of that finitely generated algebra gives a finite extension k' by the Nullstellensatz, and since X_{k'} is a closed subscheme of X_i it is quasi-affine, whence X is quasi-affine by descent along the finite locally free morphism X_{k'} to X (proof lines 2800-2813). The claim is H2: four cited inputs arranged so that quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are available before the limit argument is applied.
